title: Ki for people, mi for things

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: You already know two small question words: *ki* asks about a person and *mi* asks about a thing. *Ki ez?* – *Ez Anna.* *Mi ez?* – *Ez egy könyv.*

sections.title: Questions and answers
sections.content: The new words *kérdés* (“question”) and *válasz* (“answer”) are things, so they go with *mi*: *Mi ez? – Ez egy kérdés.* The people who ask and answer go with *ki*: *Ki kérdez? Ki válaszol?*

items.english: Who is this? – This is Meg.
What is this? – This is a question.
Who is asking? – Anna is asking.

sections.content: *Kérdez* is a verb (“to ask”) and *kérdés* is a noun (“question”). They share a root, so they are easy to mix up. The same goes for *válaszol* (“to answer”) and *válasz* (“answer”).
